_doc: Ownership manifest for the mutation-authority campaign (plans 0042-0050). This is TOOLING/GOVERNANCE metadata, not sweepable game content, which is why it lives in tools/ and not data/. It is the SINGLE home for exact ownership facts: authority classes, protected fields, construction allowances, and temporary legacy writers. Code headers and systems docs point HERE; they must not copy these lists. Enforced by tools/validate_mutation_authority.gd, whose header documents the detected write forms and the known blind spots.
_schema_rules: ONE FIELD, ONE AGGREGATE. 'Class.field' may be claimed once across the whole manifest; a second claim fails E_DUPLICATE_CLAIM. The check spans sections, so owned_models and hosted_fields cannot split the same field between two aggregates.

owned_models = this aggregate owns the WHOLE model, and every mutable field it declares must appear in 'fields' or the gate fails E_UNCLASSIFIED_FIELD. Adding a field to such a model is therefore a manifest change too.

hosted_fields = fields this aggregate owns on a model SHARED with another aggregate; no exhaustiveness requirement. Registering ONE class under hosted_fields in TWO aggregates with DISJOINT field sets is legal and supported — it is how SealiftCohort splits troops (force: bn_ids) from hulls (sealift_fleet: hulls_by_type, cohort_state), and how GameStateData is shared.

The gate resolves the RECEIVER'S TYPE before judging a write, so protection only reaches fields on a TYPED object. Values inside an untyped Dictionary/Array are invisible (the validator header's aliased-container blind spot) — that is why a shared aggregate object is made a typed Resource before its fields are registered.

Field NAMES are what get protected, and an unresolvable receiver writing a protected NAME is reported as a backstop. Prefer distinctive names: 'cohort_state' rather than 'state', which is used all over this codebase for unrelated things.

construction_writers / legacy_writers list 'path' plus exact 'Class.field' symbols. An allowance that no longer writes anything fails E_STALE_ALLOWANCE, so removing the last write means removing the entry; legacy_writers additionally require a removal_plan.

aggregates.summary: The Green anti-ship establishment: surviving launchers, permanent losses (IJFS and launch attrition), and temporary suppression, held as AntishipSystem rows plus the container-level projection the IJFS targets.

owned_models._doc: Owned model: EVERY mutable field must be classified below or the gate fails. Lifetimes: identity = fixed at construction; establishment = original strength; campaign = persists across turns; transient = reset each turn/crossing.

hosted_fields._doc: Fields this aggregate owns on a model SHARED with other aggregates. Only the listed fields are protected; GameStateData's remaining fields are claimed by plans 0044-0049.

construction_writers.why: load_systems() initialises FRESH, unpublished AntishipSystem rows from the grouping spec before anything holds them. It never accepts live establishment state.

aggregates.summary: The force aggregate migration: brigade roster, runtime placement/activity, placement-index writes, air-insertion pool/landed, and mobilization pending/released are routed through ForceTransitions. Caps/history on AirInsertionState are companion updates by ReinforcementPhases and are NOT registered here.

owned_models._doc: Plan 0044 slice: pending and released are force aggregate fields (drained/appended by ForceTransitions).

hosted_fields._doc: Plan 0044 slice: pool and landed are force aggregate fields (drained/updated by ForceTransitions). caps, history, initial_caps, first_turn are companion/identity fields excluded from this aggregate.
Plan 0044 SEA-TRANSPORT remainder: ship_reserve troop membership (BN ids in entries) is protected. JLSF cargo pseudo-entries (cargo='jlsf') are companion and exempt from force validation.

Plan 0044 SEA-TRANSPORT remainder: mainland_pool and the cohorts array (which cohorts exist) are force aggregate fields, drained/appended by ForceTransitions. The hull queues on the same model — return_pipeline, escort_sam, escort_sam_max, escort_sam_threshold, escort_reload — are claimed by the sealift_fleet aggregate (plan 0045).
Runtime placement index projection; construction and reset also route through ForceTransitions so the host file has no writer exemption.
Runtime force fields protected during plan 0044. Identity/OOB fields remain construction-only source data and are not registered to avoid generic id/name false positives.
Force authority protects surviving battalion quantities; type is identity loaded from OOB data.

Plan 0045 typed cohorts: who is ABOARD one in-transit ship group. The hulls in the same cohort (hulls_by_type) and the leg it is on (cohort_state) belong to the sealift_fleet aggregate — one object, two authorities, split by field.

construction_writers.why: load_brigades()/load_scenario() construct fresh Brigade resources and initial placement facts from OOB/scenario data before runtime play mutates them.
build() constructs a FRESH AirInsertionState from scenario data before any runtime play mutates it.
build() constructs a FRESH MobilizationState from scenario data before any runtime play mutates it.
build() constructs a FRESH SealiftState from scenario data before any runtime play mutates it.
The sent()/offloading() factories fill a FRESH cohort from a caller's plan before it is appended to any SealiftState. A cohort in flight is never rewritten here.

aggregates.summary: The hull side of the amphibious lift (plan 0045): the ShipState fleet projection (which bucket every surviving hull of a type is in) and the persistent hull queues SealiftState holds. Its counterpart is the 'force' aggregate, which owns who is ABOARD a cohort; this one owns what FLOATS. A cohort is shared by field, never reached across.

owned_models._doc: Owned model: EVERY mutable field must be classified below or the gate fails. ShipState is wholly a fleet projection, so no other aggregate has a claim on any of its fields. Lifetimes: identity = fixed at construction; establishment = the hulls the scenario starts with; campaign = persists across turns; projection = recomputed from SealiftState on every fleet write.

hosted_fields._doc: The fleet dictionary (ship name -> ShipState) itself. Replacing it is a scenario reset, which routes through SealiftTransitions.rebuild_fleet so the host file earns no writer exemption.

The hull queues on the model the force aggregate shares (plan 0045). mainland_pool and cohorts are the force aggregate's troop-side fields and are claimed there; these five are the hull side. The hull counts INSIDE a cohort are not a field of their own — they live in untyped cohort dictionaries the scanner cannot see into, which is what plan 0045's typed-cohort step exists to fix.

Plan 0045 typed cohorts: what FLOATS in one in-transit ship group and which leg it is on. bn_ids on the same model is the force aggregate's. cohort_state is spelled out rather than 'state' because the gate protects field NAMES and 'state' is used everywhere else in this codebase for something unrelated.

construction_writers.why: The sent()/offloading() factories fill a FRESH cohort from a caller's plan before it is appended to any SealiftState. Hull counts of a cohort in flight are only ever changed by SealiftTransitions.

build() seeds each escort type's SAM magazine at its scenario loadout while assembling a FRESH SealiftState, before anything holds it. The magazine is left empty when the scenario does not model reload.

build() constructs a FRESH ShipState per ship definition, all hulls ready, before anything holds the fleet. It never accepts live fleet state; replacing a LIVE fleet goes through SealiftTransitions.rebuild_fleet.

aggregates.summary: Persistent IJFS campaign state: the target list and every target's lifecycle (detection, posture, intel lock, suppression, destruction, MANPADS stock), Red munition magazines, Red squadron strength, and the day-to-day continuity of all three.

owned_models._doc: Owned model: EVERY mutable field must be classified below or the gate fails. manpads_remaining is the typed MANPADS stock plan 0046 lifted out of `metadata`; the metadata key of the same name is a serialization mirror the authority keeps in step, because metadata is aliased live into the ledger rows.
Owned model. Only inventory_remaining moves at runtime; the rest is content.

Owned model. losses_today is CAMPAIGN-cumulative despite its name — nothing resets it, and it is serialized into the air_oob_after ledger. rtb_today has no runtime writer at all and must not gain one; both are pinned by tests/ijfs/ijfs_authority_characterization_test.gd.

hosted_fields._doc: The three containers that persist across days (IjfsDailyState.gd's own header says so). The per-run ledgers and AD-health snapshots on the same object are rewritten wholesale by every run_daily and are outputs, not campaign state, so they are deliberately unregistered.
The IJFS handles GameStateData hosts. last_ijfs_summary / last_ijfs_writeback are phase OUTPUTS and stay unregistered, like every other phase summary.

construction_writers.why: Builds FRESH target/munition/squadron rows from the content files before anything holds them, and enriches SAM scores on rows still inside IjfsStateBuilder.build. It never accepts live campaign state.
Assembles the IjfsDailyState containers inside build(); nothing holds the state until it returns.

legacy_writers.why: apply_detection_ids still stamps the detection result directly; plan 0046 commit 6 routes it.
Warmup posture override and exquisite-intel lock still assign directly; plan 0046 commit 6.
resolve_strike still applies its own destroy/suppress outcome; plan 0046 commit 6.
SEAD outcomes and the return-fire/free-shot squadron losses still apply directly; plan 0046 commits 5-6.
set_remaining holds the stock and its mirror, and the island-wide contest applies squadron losses; plan 0046 commits 5-6 move both bodies into the authority.
carry_to_next_day still clears the per-day target flags directly; plan 0046 commit 6.
Activity posture and maneuver-target retirement still write directly; plan 0046 commit 6.
